-- Get carbon atoms in carcinogenic molecules
carbon_atoms AS (
    SELECT 
        a.atom_id,
        a.molecule_id
    FROM atom a
    JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
    WHERE a.element = 'c' AND m.label = '+'
),
-- Build connected carbon paths avoiding cycles
carbon_paths AS (
    SELECT 
        ca.atom_id AS start_atom,
        ca.atom_id AS current_atom,
        ca.molecule_id,
        1 AS chain_length,
        '|' || ca.atom_id || '|' AS visited_path
    FROM carbon_atoms ca
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        cp.start_atom,
        c.atom_id2 AS current_atom,
        cp.molecule_id,
        cp.chain_length + 1,
        cp.visited_path || c.atom_id2 || '|'
    FROM carbon_paths cp
    JOIN connected c ON cp.current_atom = c.atom_id
    JOIN carbon_atoms ca2 ON c.atom_id2 = ca2.atom_id
    WHERE c.atom_id2 <> cp.start_atom
      AND INSTR(cp.visited_path, '|' || c.atom_id2 || '|') = 0
),
-- Get maximum chain length per molecule
max_chains AS (
    SELECT 
        molecule_id,
        MAX(chain_length) AS max_chain_length
    FROM carbon_paths
    GROUP BY molecule_id
    HAVING MAX(chain_length) > 4
)
-- Select molecules with ranking
SELECT 
    mc.molecule_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mc.max_chain_length DESC) AS rank
FROM max_chains mc
ORDER BY mc.max_chain_length DESC;
